sources.entry: FanPilot - Fan control and temperature monitor for Apple Silicon Macs: menu bar temps, manual, max, Auto Boost rules or custom curves, with a fail-safe helper and a CLI. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/zyvren/FanPilot) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: FanPilot is a macOS menu bar app and CLI for monitoring every temperature sensor on Apple Silicon Macs and controlling fan speed (manual, max, Auto Boost rules, or custom curves) through a root helper daemon.
summary.what_it_does: FanPilot shows live temperatures in the macOS menu bar and in a sensors window grouped by area (CPU cores, GPU, SoC, battery, SSD, and others). It lets you set each fan to System, Manual (RPM or %), Max, Auto Boost (speed up when a chosen sensor passes a limit, with separate rules for battery and power adapter), or a temperature curve you draw. A privileged helper, fanpilotd, is the only component that writes fan settings; it clamps targets to the fan's hardware limits, releases fans back to macOS when the app quits, crashes, or the Mac sleeps, and forces full speed at 95 °C. The fanpilotctl command-line tool can list fans, print sensors, watch live values, set speeds with holds, and return control to macOS. Sensor reading needs no privileges. Notifications, CSV logging, and launch at login are also included.
use_cases: monitor Mac temperatures in the menu bar
control fan speed on an Apple Silicon Mac
cool a Mac during long renders or compiles
set custom fan curves based on temperature
check battery health and sensor diagnostics
log temperatures and fan speeds to CSV
notable: Privileged helper daemon is the only writer to fans, with leased control that reverts to macOS on quit, crash, or sleep
Thermal failsafe forces both fans to full speed when CPU, GPU or SoC reaches 95 °C on two samples in a row
Auto Boost rules per power source with hysteresis and an Auto Max variant
fanpilotctl CLI for scripted sensor reads and fan control
Per-model sensor name table for Apple Silicon Macs with a fallback classifier
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or later; MacBook Air and other fanless Macs get monitoring only
Not notarized by Apple, so macOS shows a warning on first launch; fan control requires installing the root helper with an administrator password
Fan control verified only on one model (MacBook Pro M5 Pro); other models are untested, and Intel support is untested
keywords: m1 m2 m3 m4 m5 mac
